headline: Digital billboard near 692 Millbury Street continued to December 21 after public comments
summary: The applicant asked to convert the south-facing side of a two-sided billboard on Route 146 into a digital display. A public speaker asked the board to deny it, citing the purpose of the Blackstone River Parkway Sign Overlay District. The next hearing is December 21st, with a constructive deadline of January 12th. The board also approved a lot split at 118 Dana Avenue and a porch variance at 538 Grove Street.
decisions: Continued the 167 and 177 Southwest Cutoff special permit hearing to November 30, 2026, and extended the constructive deadline to December 22, 2026.
Postponed the hearings for 14 to 18 Clara Drive, 209 Lincoln Street, 195 Mill Street, and 18 Crown Street to November 30, 2026, with the constructive deadline extended to December 22, 2026.
Continued the digital billboard request near 692 Millbury Street to the December 21st meeting, with a constructive deadline of January 12th, by a 4-1 vote.
Approved a 2.9 ft front yard setback variance for a front porch at 538 Grove Street, with the staff conditions and waivers, by a roll call with all votes in favor.
Approved variances to split 118 Dana Avenue into two lots and build a semi-detached two-family house, with the staff conditions and waivers, by a roll call with all votes in favor.
discussion: Digital billboard request: The applicant said the display would run only after dark and dim sharply between the 20 and 40 degree angles. Staff added conditions for city messages with 24 to 36 hours of notice, and speakers asked the board to deny the request, citing the overlay district's purpose.

118 Dana Avenue lot split: Staff said the plan needs relief from lot area, frontage, and side yard setback. Speakers raised concerns about parking, traffic, and emergency access, and the applicant's attorney said six off-street parking spaces meet the ordinance.

538 Grove Street porch: The applicant said the porch was started under an approved permit, and that the city pulled the permit after an anonymous complaint. The applicant said the porch will have railings and will not be enclosed.
